subject: Post-demo: local sample kit, auth & routing checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpath.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: platform@brightpath.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick recap + what's next for local sample kit

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the latency numbers and the routing examples really helpful. We talked internally and want to run a short local validation before committing to a dedicated pilot. High-level asks from our platform folks: 

- A minimal sample app (Python + TS) that demonstrates auth (API key + optional OIDC), per-route model routing, and a structured output/tool-calling example.
- Exact env vars and local infra (docker-compose / small k8s manifest) so we can run everything without cloud access.
- Guidance on embeddings for search + a quick reranker pipeline example (we use ElasticSearch).

Can you put together a short checklist and a starter repo we can run in our office laptop lab? If possible, include a one-page security note on data handling. I've attached our infra requirements doc.

Target timeline: get running locally by next Wednesday (26 Jul). Let me know who on your side will own the tech handoff.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform
BrightPath

Attachment: brightpath-infra-reqs.pdf (pdf, 72KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap + what's next for local sample kit

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks and the infra doc. I'm happy to own the tech handoff and will coordinate with Marissa and Priyom for the sample apps. Quick plan: 

1) Deliverables by Tue EOD (26 Jul) — starter repo with:
   - Python sample (FastAPI) and TypeScript sample (Next.js API route) showing:
     * API key auth (env-driven)
     * OIDC sketch (config + test redirect)
     * per-route model routing (route A -> text-generation, route B -> embeddings + reranker)
   - docker-compose for local runtime that boots a light Redis for KV cache + an nginx reverse-proxy for routing.
   - structured-output/tool-calling example: a small lambda-style tool that returns JSON actions and a runner in the Python sample.

2) Security note: short markdown on data retention, local logs, and what to mask before sharing.

3) Walkthrough call: Wed 26 Jul 10:00 AM PT (propose) — 30 minutes to run through repo and run locally.

If that timeline works, we'll attach a small test script you can run (smoke tests) and a checklist.

Cc'ing Marissa and Priyom for implementation items and to capture any infra constraints.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: samplekit-readme.md (stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap + what's next for local sample kit

+1 on the plan. Implementation notes and constraints from my side: 

- Auth: we'll include a lightweight API key middleware and an example OIDC provider config (Auth0 dev tenant example). OIDC will be optional and behind a feature flag.
- Routing: we will implement a simple reverse-proxy that routes by path prefix (/gen, /embed, /tools). The python sample will show runtime policy: fast route -> low-latency small model; fallback route pointing to a quantized variant.
- Embeddings + reranker: output pipeline will be: embed -> store vectors locally (we'll use FAISS in the docker-compose) -> simple BM25 fallback using a small Elastic container for hybrid search. We'll include a tiny TS reranker example that calls the Redwood API (local endpoint) and reorders results.
- Structured output/tool calling: we'll include an example where generator returns {"action":"lookup_price","args":{"sku":"..."}} and a tool-runner executes the lookup against a stub inventory service.

Attachments I'll add to the repo: smoke-test.sh, compose.yml, README with env list and the security note. Priyom — can you wire the sample testing harness and the smoke tests?

Marissa
Staff Engineer, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 3:18 PM karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> Samantha — thanks for the clear asks and the infra doc...

From: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation notes + test harness

All — I've sketched the smoke-test flow and local expectations:

- Prereqs: Docker 20+, Node 16+, Python 3.10, >=4GB RAM for the stack.
- compose.yml will launch: redis, postgres (sample data), faiss_service (python mini), elasticsearch, nginx, sample-python, sample-ts.
- smoke-test.sh steps:
  1) curl /health for each service
  2) POST /auth with API_KEY -> expect 200
  3) POST /gen with sample prompt -> expect JSON with 'text' and optionally 'action'
  4) POST /embed -> get vector and then search -> verify reranker reorders results

I'm attaching the initial smoke-test and a checklist in the repo. A few clarification points for BrightPath:
- Will you be able to run Docker with 4GB RAM in your laptop lab? If not, we can provide a reduced 'minimal' compose that swaps Elastic for a JSON file index.
- Do you have an existing OIDC provider or should we use a dev tenant?

I'll prepare the smoke-test PR and link it here.

Priyom
Developer Tools
Redwood Inference

Attachment: smoke-test.sh (bash script)

Samantha
